rulings.barItem: a stated cause that never happens, and a promise never kept
rulings.reason: The outline promises acts that customer-life.json never takes. Its nine steps are all HTTP calls by one actor, and step 1 configures a cluster, macros and logs but no users. Missing: the operator configuring users; a connection over native TCP (clickhouse.com/docs/resources/develop-contribute/native-protocol/protocol); 'A second connection reads that same record'; the readonly-GET, unknown-cluster and unsupported-engine refusals; the whole Plausible CE act (three XML bind files, the entrypoint's user-generation branch); and the read-only-profile user of paragraph 4 (clickhouse.com/docs/operations/settings/settings-users).
rulings.correction: Rewrite the outline so it narrates only the acts the life takes, in the life's order: the operator configures the local cluster; the application checks the server, creates its database and migration tables, reads the applied migrations and records one. Any act the outline keeps, such as a second reader over native TCP, appears in the life as its own steps.

rulings.barItem: a refusal without a cause the story shows, or the same cause drawn twice; a run of refusals
rulings.reason: The outline lists refusals that no act in the story causes: 'A readonly GET cannot create or insert'; 'An unknown cluster or unsupported engine is refused'; a client setting readonly to zero; an operator policy (including a later configuration door call) that tries to weaken the source file; and a mode-1 changed setting refused with 164, alongside an unchanged value and an unresolved comparison. Nothing in the story has the application send DDL by GET, name a cluster it never configured, choose an unsupported engine, or try to lift its own readonly profile. Taken together this is a run of refusals and a tour of the readonly modes on the HTTP interface page (clickhouse.com/docs/interfaces/http, GET is readonly) and the permissions-for-queries page (clickhouse.com/docs/operations/settings/permissions-for-queries).
rulings.correction: Remove these refusals from the customer's story. Keep at most one, and only where an act in the story causes it, with a cause not drawn anywhere else.

rulings.barItem: the wrong actor or credential for an act
rulings.reason: Paragraph 3 makes 'identify the actual image entrypoint bytes, and apply its exact user-generation branch' an act of the customer. Those acts belong to the image's entrypoint (spec/recordings/clickhouse-24.12.6.70-entrypoint.sh.txt) and to the twin's own source verification, not to a person or an application. Paragraphs 3 and 4 also narrate the twin's gaps ('a missing one keeps startup refused', 'an unresolved comparison names its gap', 'stay named gaps'), which are not acts at all. The vendor's configuration page (clickhouse.com/docs/operations/configuration-files) describes an operator who mounts files and starts a server. It does not describe a customer who authenticates entrypoint bytes.
rulings.correction: Give every act in the outline to an operator or the application doing what that actor does with ClickHouse, such as mounting the XML files and starting the server. Move the twin's verification and gap statements out of the outline into spec/SOURCE.md, which already holds them.
